svg.title: Filing Gates Under the IDR Operations Final Rule
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-operations-rule-filing-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Filing Gates Under the IDR Operations Final Rule; subtitle: Four checks before a dispute reaches the portal; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: For elective anesthesia, was the facility in-network?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stop the filing; check network status, admission type, and timelines and be the goalie.; gate: G2; question: Is the case keyed to the pre- or post-November 1, 2026 tracker by open-negotiation start date?; pass next: G3; fail action: Split the caseload into two calendar-based tracking systems before proceeding.; gate: G3; question: Does the batch hold 50 line items or fewer with no mix of eligible and ineligible Category I CPT codes?; pass next: G4; fail action: Rebuild the batch by manual cross-reference to avoid automatic rejection.; gate: G4; question: Is the filing inside the 4-business-day window after the 30-business-day cooling-off period with the current $15 administrative fee verified?; pass next: File the dispute and run the 30-calendar-day award-payment tracker; fail action: Escalate immediately; the portal blocks late filings with no grace period and wrong fees deny the offer.; caption: The May 28, 2026 operations final rule changes the plumbing, and each gate guards against an expired or rejected case.; assumptions note: The batch cap applies to open negotiations starting on or after November 1, 2026; practitioners split on whether the prior cap was 25 or unlimited.; note: Attributed to The Phia Group, LLC (ksxW878eWWk), Xpert Billing Talk (g3C-DoM_9CI), and HaloMD (of6CD7esHY0).

text.title: Filing Gates Under the IDR Operations Final Rule
text.tspan: Filing Gates Under the IDR Operations Final Rule

circle.title: gate: G1; question: For elective anesthesia, was the facility in-network?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stop the filing; check network status, admission type, and timelines and be the goalie.

gate: G2; question: Is the case keyed to the pre- or post-November 1, 2026 tracker by open-negotiation start date?; pass next: G3; fail action: Split the caseload into two calendar-based tracking systems before proceeding.

gate: G3; question: Does the batch hold 50 line items or fewer with no mix of eligible and ineligible Category I CPT codes?; pass next: G4; fail action: Rebuild the batch by manual cross-reference to avoid automatic rejection.

gate: G4; question: Is the filing inside the 4-business-day window after the 30-business-day cooling-off period with the current $15 administrative fee verified?; pass next: File the dispute and run the 30-calendar-day award-payment tracker; fail action: Escalate immediately; the portal blocks late filings with no grace period and wrong fees deny the offer.

text.title: Assumptions: The batch cap applies to open negotiations starting on or after November 1, 2026; practitioners split on whether the prior cap was 25 or unlimited.
